messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert — burst of OOMs (CUDA OOM) on infer-pool 'dedicated-gpu-a'. autoscaler flapping, ~8 nodes cycling. affected routes: /v1/generate (503s). tagging #eng-runtime and #eng-oncall :rotating_light:
ashley: seeing the same in metrics, KV cache resident size creeping on a subset of nodes. timeline: small leak -> fragmentation -> OOMs during long-context chattiness.
sam: logs from node gpu-13 show repeated paged allocator failures, here's a snippet:
```
2024-08-01T14:32:10Z infer: alloc_pages: failed for slab=kv_slots size=24MB, ret=-12
2024-08-01T14:32:11Z cuda: cuCtxAttach failed: out of memory
2024-08-01T14:32:11Z runtime: pod crashloop exit 137
```
raj: is this the paged-attn allocator or the legacy KV slab?
emily: customer ops — seeing increased 503s for customers: acme-search, platsync. CS on call notified, ticket created INC-4523.
sam: looks like paged-attn allocator (new path) with slot ratcheting + fragmented free lists. low-rate leak over days pushed some pages into resident set; eviction not reclaiming because of fragmented alignment. when sequence lengths spike we hit OOM.
ashley: mitigation steps I can run now: 1) bump kv eviction aggressiveness on pool to force defrag 2) cordon + drain worst nodes 3) rollout emergency config to disable paging (fallback to smaller KV)
luis: estimated customer impact: ~6% of requests in that pool hitting 503, primarily long-context chat customers. billing unaffected but SLAs breached for some enterprise customers.
ashley: executing step 1: increasing evict threshold from 0.65 -> 0.45 for dedicated-gpu-a (will monitor).
sam: also rolling a targeted restart for pods on gpu-11/gpu-13 after quiesce to flush KV cache. doing a staggered restart to avoid capacity hole.
raj: add a temporary traffic shift: route new sessions away from dedicated-gpu-a to dedicated-gpu-b until healthy. ops runbook step 4 covers this.
emily: CS notified enterprise POC for acme-search, letting them know we have an active mitigation and ETA for stabilization.
incident-bot: deployment event: rolled config evict-threshold change to pool dedicated-gpu-a by ashley at 2024-08-01T14:40:02Z.
ashley: evict threshold change in; starting pod restarts (1 every 30s). watching OOM counts.
sam: quick grep over metrics: node gpu-13 OOMs dropped from 6/min to 0.4/min after restart of 3 pods. latency for /v1/generate improved ~25ms p50.
luis: CS reports 503s trending down; still some customer retries failing.
raj: I'm preparing a short hotfix PR to opportunistically coalesce free slot chains on eviction; will open the PR and tag relnotes. but that's not safe to roll to prod mid-incident without more validation.
ashley: next steps for on-call handoff: leave pool in evict-aggressive mode, keep staggered restarts until steady for 30m, keep traffic shifted; collect heap+kv snapshots from two affected nodes (gpu-11, gpu-13) and upload to storage.
emily: created incident brief for customers: INC-4523/status updated.
ashley: handing off to sam for night follow-up. summary for next on-call: cause = paged-attn allocator fragmentation + slow kv leak; mitigation = aggressive eviction + staggered restarts + traffic shift; remaining work = collect artifacts, validate defrag hotfix, plan safe rollout. :white_check_mark:
sam: ack — I'll pick this up. leaving debug flags enabled and retention set to 72h on snapshots. if OOMs reappear, escalate to eng-runtime lead @raj.
incident-bot: thread closed for active responders at 2024-08-01T15:01:45Z (handed off).
